newsitem.title: CHINA: Migrant army shrinks in China's Shenzhen.
newsitem.headline: Migrant army shrinks in China's Shenzhen.

text.p: The ranks of migrant workers in China's southern boomtown of Shenzhen has dwindled in the last two years due in part to an exodus of labour-intensive enterprises, the Xinhua news agency said on Monday.
The army of rural Chinese who have flooded Shenzhen in search of higher-paying jobs fell to 1.74 million at the end of 1996 compared with a record 2.05 million in 1994, Xinhua said.
Their numbers had swollen by as much as 200,000 a year before the latest shift in migration trends.
Xin Benlan, deputy director of the municipal labour bureau, linked the decline to some workers being unsuited to the needs of high technology businesses, the news agency said.
Many labour-intensive enterprises had moved out of Shenzhen, Xinhua said.
It gave no statistics but Shenzhen, which borders the British colony of Hong Kong, is no longer able to compete for labour intensive production.
Inland areas boast lower labour and land costs and now offer similar incentives to those of Shenzhen, one of China's five special economic zones.
Surplus farm labour has poured into many Chinese cities in search of work shunned by affluent urban residents.
Official statistics put the number of migrants nationwide at around 80 million, but population experts believe another 20 million could have gone unreported.
